review_candidates.title: Programme Manager - Transport
review_candidates.description: At Hamilton City Council, our people are united by a shared purpose: helping make Hamilton the best place to live, work, and play. As one of New Zealand's largest city councils, we're proud to serve a growing and vibrant community while delivering services and projects that improve the wellbeing of Hamiltonians every day. You'll join a team that values collaboration, innovation, and community impact. Together, we're on track to being one of New Zealand's leading community-focused councils, where everyone matters and every contribution helps shape the future of our city. If you're looking for meaningful work, a supportive team, and the opportunity to make a real difference in your community, you'll find it here. Job Description He angituutanga: The opportunity Reporting to the Head of Portfolio Delivery, this is a key leadership role where you will guide the successful delivery of funded and emerging transport infrastructure programmes. You’ll play an important part in shaping how programmes are set up, sequenced, delivered and closed, ensuring benefits are clearly defined, risks are well managed, and outcomes are achieved for the community. As Programme Manager – Transport , you will work closely with business owners, project teams, internal specialists and external partners to provide clear programme direction and oversight. You’ll bring strong transport sector knowledge, sound judgement and the ability to influence across a complex stakeholder environment, including central government partners such as NZTA/Waka Kotahi. This role would suit someone who is confident leading complex transport programmes, understands funding pathways and business case processes, and can bring people together around a shared vision. You’ll be trusted to look ahead, identify opportunities and risks, and help ensure the programme is delivered in a way that is practical, commercially aware and aligned to long-term transport outcomes. Some key responsibilities include : Build and maintain a programme resource plan (internal and external) that supports efficient and effective programme delivery Develop and mentor Project Managers, building capability, consistency and accountability across project planning, risk management and forecasting. Lead and develop project teams with clear expectations, accountability and performance measures Drive a culture of planning discipline and continuous improvement to ensure programme forecasts, risks, dependencies and benefits are understood and accurately reported. Establish and maintain programme controls, reporting standards and assurance processes that improve the quality and reliable programme data to support informed decision making. Lead the delivery of a capital programme, providing overall direction, integration and oversight across multiple projects delivered by project managers Monitor programme performance across cost, schedule, risk and quality, with project managers responsible for project-level controls and planning team members providing analytics, estimating and reporting support Provide high-level oversight of commercial and contract management activities, including compensation events, payment claims, supplier performance, and commercial risk supported by the commercial and contracts team Lead programme-level change control and escalation, maintaining governance visibility of emerging trends and required decision points Qualifications Oo puumanawa me oo wheako | Your skills and experience At least 7 years’ experience in transport infrastructure programme or project management, with a strong understanding of local government delivery environments. Established relationships with NZTA/Waka Kotahi and the ability to work confidently across central and local government transport funding and delivery settings. Solid, in-depth understanding of NZTA funding mechanisms, including the National Land Transport Programme (NLTP), business case requirements, and pre-implementation and implementation funding cycles. A curious mind with a continuous improvement drive and comfort with ambiguity. Proven leadership skills with demonstrated ability to business partner and take people on a change journey. Demonstrated success in leading significant projects and programmes of work in the transport space. Ability to innovate and maintain a big-picture focus within an operational context. Highly developed interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work effectively with a diverse range of stakeholders (internal and external). Political acumen – the ability to engage with and influence Elected Members. Advanced written communication and presentations. Skilled in consulting with other cultural and community groups that have vested interests. Ability to operate independently, anticipate requirements and monitor workload. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills. Financial analysis skills. Tertiary qualification in Project Management and /or Civil Engineering fields Project Management, Programme Management training. Project management accreditation (for example, PRINCE2 or PMP) or equivalent (preferred, but not essential). Understanding of obligations of local and central government under the Treaty of Waitangi. Current full driver’s license. Additional Information He aha te wariu o te utu kaimahi? | What’s the salary? Circa $140k dependent on skills and experience. Ngaa waahi whakarato painga kei a maatou: What we offer We invest in our people, their wellbeing, and their future. That's why we offer a range of benefits designed to support you both inside and outside of work, including: We support flexible ways of working that balance individual wellbeing, team and business needs. And great outcomes for our community. We support professional development and opportunities to grow your career. Two wellbeing days each year to focus on what matters most to you (after one year of service). Fully funded Unimed health insurance, including hospital and surgical cover, with discounted rates for family members. Free annual health checks and flu vaccinations. The option to purchase additional annual leave for greater flexibility. Eye care support, including reimbursement towards eye testing and prescription glasses. Access to a wide range of local discounts, including gyms, cafes, healthcare providers, retail stores, and more. Me Tono Inaaianei!: Apply Now! View the position description. Click apply ​Complete your application. If you wish to include a cover letter with your application, please combine this in the same file as your resume and upload as a PDF file. Alternatively, you can use the 'Write a message to the Hiring Team' text box. Applications close on the: 18 October 2026 Note: We will be shortlisting as we receive applications. Council is committed to honouring the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi/Treaty of Waitangi through its relationship with Kiingitanga, Waikato Tainui, mana whenua and maataa waka within Hamilton Kirikiriroa. All candidates will be notified of the outcome on their application via email. Short-listed candidates will be required to complete an interview process, reference checks and a criminal check. Further background checking will be required when relevant to the role. View more information about these checks, our commitment to the Privacy act and details for international applicants by clicking here It is important to us that we support you throughout our selection process (interview and assessments). If you have any access needs during this process, let us know in advance so we can make sure these are met. As a council, we believe in creating a welcoming environment where everyone feels valued and belongs. We value inclusiveness (Kotahitanga) – we respect and value the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents that everyone brings. This role is being sourced directly. If/where Hamilton City Council requires the support of a recruitment agency, we will seek this support from our panel of selected agencies. Hamilton City Council will not be responsible for, and will not pay, any commissions, fees or other payments related to unsolicited contact.

review_candidates.description: Senior leadership role shaping regional natural resource management outcomes Lead Reef Catchments' Land & Water portfolio across the region Mackay or Proserpine based role with broad stakeholder engagement The Organisation Our client, Reef Catchments is the natural resource management (NRM) organisation for the Mackay Whitsunday Isaac region. They work with landholders, Traditional Owners, industry, community groups, researchers and government to improve the region's land, water and biodiversity. Their projects deliver practical, on-ground outcomes. Whether it is improving water quality flowing to the Great Barrier Reef, restoring wetlands and habitats, supporting sustainable agriculture, or helping local communities care for the environment, they are focused on projects that make a real difference across our region. The Role Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Program Director, Land and Water provides strategic leadership, portfolio governance and delivery assurance across Reef Catchments’ Land and Water program. The role leads Managers and program teams to translate strategic priorities and funding commitments into coordinated, safe and effective delivery with measurable regional outcomes. This is a broad senior leadership role combining strategy, program and project assurance, financial oversight, people leadership, investment development and high-level stakeholder engagement. Key Roles and Responsibilities Provide strategic direction and leadership across the Land and Water portfolio, including Waterways, Sustainable Agriculture and other allocated functions. Oversee complex programs and projects, ensuring scope, budgets, schedules, milestones, resources, risks and funding obligations are effectively managed. Provide evidence-based advice to the CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Board on performance, emerging issues, risks, opportunities and investment priorities. Lead portfolio governance, delivery assurance, risk, compliance, monitoring, evaluation and reporting. Identify and progress strategically aligned funding and investment opportunities, including proposals, business cases and delivery models. Build trusted senior relationships and represent Reef Catchments with government, funders, Traditional Owners, landholders, industry, research organisations and regional partners. About You You are an experienced senior leader who can think strategically while maintaining clear oversight of complex operational delivery. You bring sound judgement, strong governance and commercial awareness, and the ability to lead through complexity and change without becoming unnecessarily involved in routine operational decisions. Equally you will excel at leading people and empowering others to do their best work. You are known for your ability to build trust and genuine relationships across diverse stakeholder groups and can translate technical, financial and governance information into clear priorities and decisions. Natural resource management or related environmental, agricultural or regional-development experience is highly regarded, as is knowledge of the Mackay Whitsunday Isaac region and experience engaging with Traditional Owners. Required Skills and Proficiencies Relevant tertiary qualification in natural resource management, environmental science, agriculture, waterway management, project or program management, business, leadership or equivalent substantial professional experience. Demonstrated senior leadership experience across complex, multidisciplinary programs or portfolios. Proven ability to lead, mentor and uplift capability of a multi-disciplinary team. Experience overseeing multiple projects, budgets, funding agreements, delivery teams and stakeholder relationships. Strong capability in program governance, risk management, compliance and delivery assurance. Experience in workforce planning, people leadership, organisational change and capability development. Demonstrated ability to build senior relationships with government, funders, industry, landholders, delivery partners and community stakeholders. High-level communication, negotiation, judgement and decision-making skills. Ability to develop and evaluate funding proposals, business cases, project plans, budgets and performance reports, and interpret complex grants and contracts. The Rewards and Culture This is an opportunity to join Reef Catchments’ Senior Leadership Team and help shape the future of a significant regional natural resource management portfolio. This influential role offers the opportunity to guide strategic investment, strengthen delivery and partnerships, build organisational capability, and achieve lasting environmental and community outcomes across the Mackay Whitsunday Isaac region. Reef Catchments offers a collaborative and purpose-driven culture where people work together to solve complex problems, build trusted partnerships and deliver practical results. Diverse perspectives and experience are valued, supporting better decisions and stronger outcomes for the region. This is a role where you can see the tangible impact of your leadership and contribution. You will contribute to meaningful environmental and community outcomes while being supported by a range of benefits designed to promote flexibility, wellbeing and professional growth. Benefits include: Five weeks’ annual leave, additional leave over Christmas and flexible working arrangements. Career development and progression opportunities, including up to $2,000 per year for professional development. Team building and wellbeing initiatives. Retention incentives after three, five and seven years of continuous service. How to Apply Apply now by submitting your current CV (in Word format) via our online application process. For a confidential discussion or to review the PD please contact Claire Black on 0407821086 or via claire@talentnation.com.au To be eligible to apply, you must have unrestricted rights to work in Australia. Talent Nation encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and people of all cultures, abilities, sex, and genders. Applicants can request a reasonable adjustment at any stage during the recruitment process, please contact us so we can provide adjustments for you.

review_candidates.description: Who We Are AngloGold Ashanti is a global gold mining company with a diverse, high-quality portfolio of operations, projects and exploration activities across 10 countries on four continents. We pursue value-creating opportunities involving other minerals, where we can leverage our existing assets, shareholdings, skills and experience. At AngloGold Ashanti, we assure you of work that carries significance and creates tangible results. What we do goes beyond mining. We build livelihoods in communities, champion environmental stewardship, and strengthen local and national economies. Our leaders and teams are committed to listening to and supporting each other, valuing differences, and embracing equity. We are convinced that greatness only happens when we prioritize these behaviors and the well-being of every person. Learn more about our Vision, purpose, values - AngloGold Ashanti POSITION Principal, Project Civil & Structural Engineer DEPARTMENT Project Management LOCATION Johannesburg EMPLOYMENT STATUS Permanent OBJECTIVE OF THE ROLE Acts as the civil and structural discipline authority and Subject Matter Expert (SME) within the Global Projects function. The role drives technical assurance, structural integrity, and lean infrastructure practices across major Organic Growth projects from Concept through to Execution. Role Accountabilities Technical Assurance: Review and approve critical civil/structural deliverables, including bulk earthworks, dynamic machine foundations (for SAG/ball mills, crushers), structural steelwork (conveyor gantries, transfer towers), and surface water networks. Value Optimization: Challenge over-design and structural over-engineering (such as oversized concrete volumes or heavy steel profiles) using Minimum Viable Solution (MVS) and lean owner's team delivery principles. Specialist Governance: Manage and review the performance of third-party technical specialists across geotechnical engineering, seismic assessments, and hydrological modeling. Interface & EPCM Management: Direct external EPCM performance, coordinate complex cross-functional project interfaces, and support commercial packages for bulk materials and earthworks contracts. Safety Leadership: Lead and facilitate formal Safety in Design (SiD), HAZID, HAZOP, and constructability/maintainability reviews. Role Requirements Education & Qualification Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Structural Engineering Professional/Chartered Engineer registration (e.g., ECSA, CPEng, PE) Experience, Knowledge And Skills 8–10 years in mineral processing or mining infrastructure (earthworks, roads) 5 years at a Senior/Principal level within an Owner's Team managing EPCM contracts Expert knowledge of heavy industrial steelwork, soil-structure interaction, storm water management, and a value-focused mindset capable of leading global cross-functional teams without direct line authority. Benefits Summary AngloGold Ashanti offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support employees’ health, financial security, and overall well-being. Medical insurance, employee assistance programmes, and wellbeing initiatives. Company-supported pension or provident fund contributions. Annual leave, sick leave, and public holidays in line with company policy. review_candidates.description: Description Location: Remote (in the following states: Colorado, Georgia, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Mississippi, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas). Job Type: Full-Time Bridge the Gap Between Care and Coverage. Behind every successful surgery is a meticulous specialist who ensures everything is cleared and ready to go. As our Pre-Certification Surgery Specialist , you’ll be the critical link securing surgical authorizations, coordinating medical records, and keeping care on track for our patients. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, love solving insurance puzzles, and bring a strong sense of urgency to your work, this could be the role for you. Why Join Us? Collaborate with leading orthopaedic specialists in a streamlined, patient-centered setting. Ensure patients get the surgical care they need without financial or administrative delays. Enjoy comprehensive healthcare coverage, paid time off, and 401(k) options. What You'll Do Secure timely pre-certifications and pre-determinations for upcoming surgical procedures. Request and compile clinical treatment records needed for pre-service insurance reviews. Partner with insurance carriers and clinical staff to maintain smooth operations. Efficiently navigate electronic medical record systems while adhering to HIPAA standards. Requirements What You Bring: Minimum of 2 years of surgical pre-certification experience required (orthopaedics preferred). Familiarity with health insurance guidelines, Worker’s Comp, Motor Vehicle Accidents (MVA), and medical terminology. Exceptional attention to detail, a strong sense of urgency, and the ability to multitask in a high-volume environment. Proficiency in electronic medical records (EMR) software and professional communication skills across all channels. Compensation & Benefits OrthoNJ, LLC is required by New Jersey law to disclose the compensation range for this position. The hiring range for this role is $20.00-$28.00 per hour. Compensation is determined based on several factors, including but not limited to the candidate’s qualifications, relevant experience, and geographic location. Eligible full-time employees are offered a comprehensive benefits package, which may include paid time off, medical, dental, vision, and a retirement plan. Practice Introduction Princeton Orthopaedic Associates (POA), a division of OrthoNJ, is a Community of Extraordinary Care professionals serving Central New Jersey since 1974. With 30 physicians, including 20 Orthopaedic surgeons, across 7 office locations, urgent care centers, and surgical center, POA operates as an outcome-focused orthopaedic practice that combines extraordinary talent, advanced techniques, and cutting-edge tools with compassionate service. As part of New Jersey's largest independent orthopaedic group practice, POA physicians work collaboratively to provide personalized, patient-centered care while maintaining the values and autonomy of the private practice model. Princeton Orthopaedic Associates is built on a foundation of compassion, patient focus, quality, collaboration, honesty, and excellence. We are a community where every team member—regardless of role—is expected to embody these values in their daily work, hold themselves and colleagues accountable to high standards, and speak up when behavior falls short of our expectations. We foster a culture of continuous improvement where feedback is welcomed, mistakes become learning opportunities, and successes are celebrated together. As a member of our team, you'll be expected to contribute ideas, mentor new colleagues, and actively participate in creating an environment where both patients and staff thrive. EEO Disclosure POA is an equal opportunity employer. POA, as a member organization of OrthoNJ, is strongly committed to creating and preserving equal opportunity for all employees and applicants. We make all employment decisions – including recruitment, hiring, compensation, training, promotion, transfer, discipline, dismissal from employment, and other personnel matters – without regard to actual or perceived race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, genetic information, citizenship, gender identity and expression, parental status, or other legally protected characteristics or conduct.
